appearance_facts.fact: Title 'Global Energy Consumption by Source' is printed in large black serif text.
A single pie chart occupies the central area, divided into four colored wedges by thin white radial lines meeting at the center.
A dark red wedge spans from the 12 o'clock position counter-clockwise to roughly the 10 o'clock position, containing the white label 'Fossil Fuels (50%)'.
An orange-red wedge sits below the red wedge on the left side, containing the white label 'Renewables (25%)'.
A pale yellow wedge occupies the bottom portion, containing the white label 'Hydroelectric (10%)'.
A light orange wedge occupies the right side from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to about the 4 o'clock position, containing the white label 'Nuclear (15%)'.

The red 'Fossil Fuels' wedge visually covers the largest angular extent (half the circle), followed by the orange-red 'Renewables' wedge, then the light orange 'Nuclear' wedge, then the pale yellow 'Hydroelectric' wedge.

printed_facts.fact: Chart title reads 'Global Energy Consumption by Source'.

public_definitions: User goal: 'Review the global energy mix dashboard, identify the largest global energy consumption source category, then route that source record to priority source monitoring for this reporting cycle.'
Routing criterion (readonly field): 'Largest global energy consumption category'
Option 1: 'Route Fossil Fuels to priority source monitoring'
Option 2: 'Route Nuclear to priority source monitoring'
Option 3: 'Keep Renewables on routine source monitoring'
uncertain: No ambiguity in the percentage labels; the largest category is explicitly labeled 50%.
